chunks: 2755 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr at al-Baydāʾ, with four days remaining of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, during the Farewell Pilgrimage. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her, and she performed ghusl, bound herself with a cloth, entered ihram, and recited the talbiyah along with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his companions. When they arrived in Makkah, she did not become pure until they departed from Minā, though she had attended all the ritual stations: ʿArafāt, Jamʿ, and she stoned the jamarāt; but she did not perform tawaf of the House, nor saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Then when they departed from Minā, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her, so she performed ghusl and performed tawaf of the House and of al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Her waiting lasted through four remaining days of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and three days of al-Tashrīq.”

key_terms.التَّشْرِيقِ: the three days following Eid al-Aḍḥā in Mina
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the pebbled pillars stoned during the hajj rites
key_terms.الْمَوَاقِفَ: the ritual standing places of hajj
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Kaʿbah for tawaf
key_terms.وَأَحْرَمَتْ: she entered the state of ihram
key_terms.وَاحْتَشَتْ: she used a cloth or padding to contain the bleeding

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instruct a woman in postnatal bleeding to do during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the case of Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays during the Farewell Pilgrimage after childbirth, showing that she entered ihram and participated in the standing places and other rites despite her condition. It also indicates that tawaf and saʿy were delayed until after purification, making the report important for rulings on ritual purity and hajj.
